newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks close at record high on Dow rally.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks close at record high on Dow rally.

text.p: Australian stocks closed at a record high on Tuesday after a fresh high on Wall Street and strong rises in other markets in the Asia Pacific region encouraged investors.
The All Ordinaries index ended 20.1 points higher at 2,512.8 after earlier hitting a new intra-day high of 2,518.5 with A$962.41 million (US$750.68 million) worth of trade going through the market.
The Australian market has flirted with the 2,500 level over the past week but has failed to hold above that level.
"Let's face it, our market has gone up 21 points in the last two days when the Dow has gone up 250, so you can hardly say that there is a boom on," said John Bowie-Wilson, a broker at BNP Equities.

Brokers said bank stocks, which make up about 20 percent of the broader market, were boosted by a continued rally in bond yields. Australia's major banks - Westpac, ANZ and National Australia Bank - all found solid buying.
However, market leader BHP missed the market surge, ending one cent down at A$18.02 on apparent profit-taking after its recent strong run up.
The gold sector recovered most of Monday's losses which followed news of the Busang gold fraud, brokers said.
